title: Role Transition Playbook: Embedded Contractor to Full-Time Conversion
author: Elena Rossi
content:
Overview:
This playbook documents the standardized process for converting embedded contractors, consultants, or long-term vendors into Redwood Inference full-time employees (FTEs). It covers hiring approvals, technical and cultural onboarding, role-level competency checks, IT/security provisioning, compensation calibration, and a 120-day ramp to role parity. The goal is a repeatable, transparent conversion that minimizes disruption to delivery and protects security and compliance posture.

When to use this guide:
- A contractor has received a formal offer and accepted moving to an FTE role.
- A long-term vendor engagement is transitioning to an internal headcount.
- The destination team requests a full-time role to replace contractor work.

Key objectives:
- Complete all HR and security provisioning prior to first day as FTE.
- Ensure at least 3 documented artifacts and 2 knowledge-transfer sessions exist before role transfer.
- Achieve role competency checkpoints by day 30, 60, 120.

Primary stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager: sponsor the conversion, define role expectations, run technical and cultural assessment, and own 120-day ramp plan.
- People Ops: lead offer coordination, background checks, compensation calibration, and new-hire admin tasks.
- IT/Security: validate access changes and complete privileged access approval prior to start date.
- Finance: assign budget code and start-date for payroll provisioning.
- Peer Sponsor (Buddy): assigned by hiring manager to provide daily operational support for first 60 days.

Pre-offer checklist (Hiring Manager & People Ops):
1) Validate headcount and budget with Finance.
2) Verify contractor status, IP clauses, and any non-compete implications with Legal.
3) Confirm eligibility for full-time benefits and relocation needs.
4) Calibrate compensation band using banding matrix and recent comp benchmarks.
5) Prepare offer letter template and proposed start date.

Offer and acceptance (People Ops):
- Standard timeline: 3 business days for initial offer response window.
- Include: start date, compensation, title, reporting manager, benefits overview, probation period (if applicable), and relocation/visa contingencies.
- Trigger items on acceptance: background check initiation, payroll onboarding form, corporate email reservation, and badge request.

Security and legal gating (must complete before start):
- Background check clearance.
- IP assignment and contractor termination/contract amendment completed.
- Any vendor/third-party agreements reviewed such that data ownership and access policies are preserved.
- MFA and SSO provisioning plan scheduled.

Technical and operational handoff (Hiring Manager and Peer Sponsor):
- Artifact inventory: code repos, runbooks, dashboards, deployment keys, vendor accounts. List links and owners.
- 2x knowledge-transfer sessions documented (recording or written notes).
- Create an access de-escalation plan if contractor credentials need to be retired.
- Define first 30/60/120 deliverables aligned to an objective success metric (example templates below).

First-week checklist (Day 0-7):
- HR: benefits orientation, payroll confirmation, and new-hire paperwork completion.
- IT: compute device assigned, VPN/SSO access, standard toolchain installed.
- Security: privileged access exceptions (if needed) validated and logged.
- Manager: daily check-ins, buddy pairing, role expectations and success metrics reviewed.
- Team: welcome intro, stakeholder directory, and calendar invites for recurring meetings.

30/60/120 day competency milestones (examples to adapt by role):
- 30 days: Completed onboarding tasks, executed at least one end-to-end code change or deliverable with review, attended key cross-team syncs, and passed a basic ops/runbook walk-through.
- 60 days: Independently delivers on recurring tasks, demonstrates operational ownership in one area (e.g., monitoring, deploys), and contributes to planning.
- 120 days: Reaches parity with peers on productivity and code quality; leads a small project and mentors others on transferred knowledge.

Role parity assessment criteria (used at day 120):
- Technical proficiency: passes a practical review (PRs, feature ownership, incident participation).
- Process adoption: uses team workflows, ticketing, CI/CD pipeline, and observability tools.
- Collaboration: integrates into team rituals, communicates with stakeholders, and receives positive feedback from buddy and cross-functional partners.

Compensation and benefits notes:
- Contractors converting within 6 months: standard band review; manager provides justification for above-band offers.
- Contractors converting after 12+ months: include performance summary and manager endorsement for accelerated banding if applicable.
- Equity eligibility: clarified at offer time per People Ops policy; vesting start date established in offer.

Examples: First 30-day deliverable templates
1) Individual contributor (engineer): "Deliver a small bugfix or feature with automated tests and deployment runbook updated."
2) Product manager: "Author a 1-page customer problem brief and run the first prioritization triage with stakeholders."
3) Designer: "Deliver a prototype and usability notes; present to cross-functional partners for feedback."

Access and credentialing patterns (common scenarios):
- If contractor had vendor-managed credentials, issue new corporate credentials to avoid shared secrets.
- Rotate any keys or tokens used during contractor period on day 0 of FTE status.
- For sensitive systems, escalate privileges in two stages: limited access on day 1, expanded after 30-day review.

Buddy program guidance (Peer Sponsor):
- Buddy time allocation: 1 hour/day for first 2 weeks, tapering to 1-2 hours/week by week 6.
- Suggested activities: guided walkthroughs, shadowing deploys, calendar clean-up, and culture Q&A.
- Feedback: buddies submit a short 1-page onboarding summary at day 30 and day 60.

Risk controls and compliance exceptions:
- If contractor had access to customer data, require an audit of prior access and explicit re-certification before conversion.
- Any unresolved IP or contractual obligations must block offer finalization.
- For visa-sponsored contractors, coordinate early with immigration counsel; do not set start date until visa transfer is confirmed.

Manager checklist for first 120 days (summary):
- Week 1: confirm paperwork, buddy assigned, access validated, first deliverable scoped.
- Week 2-4: weekly 1:1s focused on knowledge gaps and artifacts completion.
- Month 2: 30/60 progress review and calibration with manager and people-ops.
- Month 3: 120-day parity review and final sign-off; determine any ongoing development plan.

Reporting and audit trail requirements:
- People Ops will retain conversion packet (offer, background check confirmation, IP assignment, role activation) in HRIS.
- Hiring Manager must upload artifact inventory and buddy reports to the team's onboarding folder and link to the HR packet.

Escalation paths:
- If critical access or security issues are found, notify Security and People Ops immediately; pause conversion if needed.
- For compensation disputes, People Ops and Finance mediate with documented rationale and final approval by Head of People.
